0.comment: Lan Yan: Lan Junming, the Wind Reader
0.content:
Lan Junming, called the Wind Reader, was one of the human Three Hermits of Guizang among the Eight Adepts who defeated the god Tao Dou. He first taught the Lan clan the Qimen arts. The Wuwang Kid nicknamed him "Mad Lan" (in return for being called "Red Runt") and later "Fool Lan". He was a carefree wanderer who studied whatever caught his interest, had no master, cared little for duty and invented his own arts. One of them was the Soul-Binding Art, which traps part of a soul in a rattan effigy and which the clan later forbade. In 7.1 a fragment of his soul, bound to a rattan puppet and sealed by his own hand, wandered Yilong Wharf at Moonchase saying "Moonchase ought not to be like this." Lan Yan saw through it, and with Zibai's help they identified him.

He liked Lan Yan at once and saw a fellow free spirit in her. He asked her to call him "Grandmaster" rather than "Ancestor". He told her a founder's lesson was to soar like a bird without caring what lay below, and he suggested she might one day found a clan of her own. Lan Yu explained that he never married. The modern clan descends from his elder and younger brothers, to whom he taught everything in his later years. He also never forced anyone to study and never refused a sincere outsider, and the clan still follows that rule.

His lost memory was the "seeing off of the autumn swallow". During the Archon War, Silverwing went to fight evil spirits across Liyue. He combined his Qimen arts with principles borrowed from the Wuwang Kid's Qihuang sigils into a ward that both of them carried. Each Moonchase they met at a pavilion east of Teatree Slope to renew it, and he watched her fly off after the moon. He bound his soul to keep that promise after his death. The fragment woke at Moonchase many times over the centuries, but Silverwing never came; Lan Yan concluded that each time he used the art to make himself forget. When Lan Yan told him the truth he nearly fell apart. Her farewell art released the seal, and he left content that Liyue's young people were protecting the land just as Silverwing wished.

1.comment: Lan Yan: The Jade-Plumed Silverwing and the swallows
1.content:
The Jade-Plumed Silverwing was a swallow adeptus and one of the Three Beasts of Tao Dou among the Eight Adepts. She was closely bound to the Wind Reader. Lan Yan's silver hair ornament is modelled on her, a Lan heirloom handed down so the clan never forgets its roots. Chenyu Vale treats swallows kindly, and the Lan family most of all: any swallow may nest under their eaves. Lan Yan has told the Traveler the old warnings. One says a swallow may take your place in death at the gates of Tao Dou; another, from her grandfather, says unkindness to swallows can bring an early death.

In Lan Yan's lifetime, though, swallows only rushed through Chenyu Vale without nesting. She sensed their power resonated with her clan's arts and spent years trying to find an art to bring them back, always missing a piece. In 7.1 the Wind Reader's story gave her the idea that his art for seeing swallows off and hers for welcoming them home were two forms of one art.

Zhongli told the Traveler what had happened (@version 7.1). The swallows were Silverwing's living embodiments and the source of her power. Through decades of wartime flights across Liyue, flocks died, and each lost swallow took part of her mind and memories with it. New swallows restored her strength but not her mind. By war's end the flocks had forgotten the promise, their home and even how to nest. Zhongli compared her to a ship rebuilt plank by plank, and said a new consciousness might one day arise in the flocks. After Lan Yan's art the swallows stopped rushing, and more should return to nest in Chenyu Vale.

key: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
2.comment: Lan Yan: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (7.1 Moonchase event)
2.content:
During the limited-time 7.1 Moonchase event, Chenyu Vale's associations, guided by the Lan elders, organised the festival at Yilong Wharf. It included a World Food Fair with cooks from Mondstadt, Fontaine (Escoffier) and Sumeru. Lan Yan wasn't picked to fight evil spirits with the Millelith and was happily acting as the Traveler's guide when she found the soul-bound Wind Reader. The search for "his" Moonchase led to Zibai and Zhongli, then to a Moon-Viewing Gathering at Wangshu Inn.

On the road through Dihua Marsh they joined Hu Tao, Xingqiu, Chongyun and Gaming, who were protecting Gaming's cargo from possessed monsters. Lan Yan used a clan banner to empower the fighters and sent her flying rattan figures after the escaping spirits. At Wangshu Inn they met Xiao and the Yunlai Angler's descendant (who declined to stay), then held a feast with Xiao and Xiangling where Hu Tao proposed a "New Eight". Hu Tao then recited her ancestor's winning poem about the "windborne silverwing", and the Wind Reader remembered his promise.

Lan Yan and the Traveler conjured the swallow sign on the lake, but Silverwing never came. While Lan Yan, Hu Tao and Chongyun held his fading soul together, the Traveler learned the truth from the adepti at Mt. Aocang. Lan Yan chose to tell him everything and then cast her recreated art as a farewell song. The seal dissolved, a swallow shape flew from the rattan figure, and his soul returned to the Ley Lines. Zhongli and Zibai watched from a cliff; Zhongli had tried to tell him for years. Two days later Ningguang came to thank her, and the Lan elders began talking about real training.

3.comment: Lan Yan: Springtime Charms and the border crisis (5.3)
3.content:
During the limited-time 5.3 Lantern Rite, the Ministry of Civil Affairs invited Lan Yan to Liyue Harbor to help organise a street fair. Her grandfather's longevity readings had suddenly started telling everyone they had only a few years to live, and his only clue was "Wangsheng Funeral Parlor", so she sought out Hu Tao. Following her to Wuwang Hill, Lan Yan found Qiqi blocking a crevice, and both were pulled into the border between life and death. There they met Hu Tao burning fetor. Lan Yan kept them hidden with an illusion until the Traveler and Xiao got them out.

Earlier she had left protective rattan figures with Xingqiu's ailing great-grandfather and near the sick Timaeus. Rumours spread by Tea Master Liu Su blamed the Lans for cursing the Feiyun patriarch with it, until Zhongli identified its sigil as the auspicious Sign of Vaisravana. She wrote to her main-branch cousin about whether the Sanctification of Tao Dou ritual truly needed one participant to be obscured from the Ley Lines. The cousin suspected it was a rule of the land but suggested sharing the burden.

Lan Yan tied rattan figures of Hu Tao to the gate array so Ningguang, Keqing, Ganyu, Xiao, Qiqi, Beidou, Yelan and Lan Yan herself would each absorb part of the fetor. The Ley Lines refused to link the Traveler at all, which baffled her. She held the Gate of Initiation in Liyue Harbor with Ningguang. When the fetor overwhelmed the figures, Hu Tao's broke and Lan Yan could no longer sense her. The unlinked Traveler then went in and saved Hu Tao.

4.content:
Lan Yan had heard of Director Hu but first met her face to face without realising it, while Hu Tao was out of uniform buying ritual perfume. Lan Yan was soon trapped with her in the border. She noticed that Hu Tao jokes about everything yet keeps her real plans to herself, and hopes her smiles will come from real happiness rather than from trying to reassure others. Hu Tao says Lan Yan is much stronger than she claims, and that her habit of curing fetor and illness is bad for the funeral business.

In 7.1 Hu Tao went along to help the Wind Reader. She grouped herself, Lan Yan and Chongyun as the finest of Liyue's "three great traditions" of mystic arts and the "Three Heroes of Chenli". She recited the Wuwang Kid's poem that unlocked the Grandmaster's memory, and helped Lan Yan hold his soul together. Hu Tao's ancestor and Lan Yan's Grandmaster were friendly rivals who called each other "Red Runt" and "Mad Lan".

5.content:
Gaming and Lan Yan have been friends since childhood. As a boy he trampled one of his family's baskets as a joke, and Lan Yan and her grandfather happened to visit that day to check the house's geomantic energies. She helped him repair it before he got into trouble. She remembers him as a "neighbourhood terror" who grew up, as she did. He still brings snacks wherever he goes and stocks up on hometown favourites before he leaves. He tells friends to let Lan Yan guide them to the best mountain food.

In 7.1 she helped protect Gaming's fragile cargo from possessed monsters in Dihua Marsh. He promised to treat everyone at Xinyue Kiosk. He was at her birthday mushroom feast in Chenyu Vale, where Xiangling kept most dishes mild for him and Chongyun.

6.content:
Lan Yan's first meal in Liyue Harbor was at Wanmin Restaurant. The spicy boiled fish caught her off guard, and she only wished she had come sooner to meet Xiangling. Guoba took to her instantly, and they spent ages shaking hands. She promised to take Xiangling foraging for wild mushrooms and insects in Chenyu Vale.

She kept the promise. In early 2026 she invited Xiangling, Chongyun and Gaming home, and Xiangling raced around looking for ingredients, even eyeing Lan Yan's melon vines for a cold dish. Lan Yan distracted her with mushrooms. Xiangling cooked an all-mushroom feast and made a mildly spicy stir-fry just for her. In 7.1 Xiangling invited the Traveler to the World Food Fair and cooked for the Moon-Viewing Gathering.

7.comment: Lan Yan: Keqing, Ningguang and the Qixing
7.content:
Keqing greeted Lan Yan at the 5.3 Lantern Rite as a member of the historic Lan lineage, whose ancestors came from the Twelve Tribes of Chenyu Vale. She praised her knowledge of Guyan sigils and plans to consult her as the Ministry promotes local crafts. Lan Yan wants to treat the overworked Yuheng to a meal and secretly wishes Keqing would do her hair in cat ears. With Ningguang, Lan Yan held a gate of the 5.3 ritual array.

At the 6.3 Lantern Rite she brought Ningguang and Keqing her grandfather's and elders' forecast: "On Lantern Rite, the moon shall go dark." She noted that the moon in a photograph of the anomaly sat right above Chiwang Terrace, where Chenyu Vale's ancient people were said to commune with the heavens. In 7.1 she guided Ningguang to the clan elders. Ningguang later came to thank her for the swallow art in front of her elders and told her she deserved the praise, which only made Lan Yan more nervous.

8.content:
Lan Yan keeps running into Xingqiu in the mountains on what are clearly not Feiyun Commerce Guild errands. Since then he has brought her the newest supernatural novels, on condition that she tells no one, which she then accidentally tells the Traveler. Chongyun is a fellow thaumaturge with a pure-yang body. Once she saw him leave a house call her grandfather had also read, looking dejected, and still cannot work out what happened.

Both joined the 7.1 journey to Wangshu Inn. The Wind Reader was bemused that Mt. Tianheng's exorcists never founded a sect, and that a "Guhua Clan" had taken the place he expected the Yunlai Angler's school to hold. Chongyun's ancestors are said to have learned the mystic arts from the Wind Reader. Xingqiu used the battle report to excuse a skipped lesson.

9.comment: Lan Yan: The Lan clan and Lan Yan's family
9.content:
The Lan clan is an old thaumaturge family of Chenyu Vale who practise the Qimen arts taught by the Wind Reader, and they make rattan figures for exorcism. Lan Yan was born into a branch line. Her grandfather does geomantic house calls and tells fortunes in Yilong Wharf. Her parents are warm, practical people who give her silver for every milestone. In 5.3 she said her family were only distant relatives of the main line, and that she earns more from crafts than her grandfather does from fortunes.

By 7.1 the clan helps organise Moonchase at Yilong Wharf and works with the Millelith against seasonal evil spirits. Its head is Lan Yu, whom Lan Yan calls uncle; how close her branch is to his is not explained. Members may choose the arts as a duty or a hobby. The elders, including an Aunt Lan and an Uncle Lan, are formal and stern. They forbid using the Lan name to overcharge for rattan figures and teach outsiders for little more than the cost of a few meals.

Lan Ying is a young second cousin who calls her "Big Sis" and describes Lan Yan as "my grandfather's cousin's nephew's daughter". She notes that Lan Yan recognises even very distant relatives on sight. Lan Ying learned figure-making from Lan Yan, and together they designed Warding Figures with a Qimen core that seals small clumps of evil energy. In 7.1 Lan Ying sold them at cost on the food street, and the elders offered rewards to anyone who used one to dispel evil. A separate, unnamed main-branch cousin taught Lan Yan the rattan-figure technique and advised her by letter in 5.3.

10.comment: Lan Yan: Rattan weaving and rattan figures
10.content:
Lan Yan is the Chenyu Vale Artisans Association's master rattan weaver. Chenyu Vale is famed for silversmithing, jade carving, dyeing and rattan weaving, and Mingxing Jewelry of Liyue Harbor sends buyers there. Her process: gather vines at dawn (stiff ones from old forests for screens, supple ones by the water for baskets), split the core from the skin, wash and dry them, then weave warp and weft with total focus. She makes furniture, screens, baskets, vases, hats, furniture covers and toys, and repairs heirlooms.

For the Lan clan, rattan figures are a tool of the Qimen arts. Each carries an engraved exorcism sigil that soaks up inauspicious energy around its owner and is meant to be destroyed afterwards. Lan Yan's are cuter than the old black-and-grey ones, by design. She uses them to protect the sick, link people into ritual arrays, sweep up evil spirits in flight and make portraits of friends. Her finished pieces are washed, sun-dried, shaped, planed, steamed, oiled and coloured, and she says they resist moisture and insects. She hates seeing good rattan smothered under protective cloth.

11.comment: Lan Yan: The Qimen arts and Liyue's thaumaturges
11.content:
In Liyue, "thaumaturges" are mortals who preserve mystic arts learned from the adepti or worked out themselves. Ningguang names the Wuwang Kid (founder of the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor) and the Wind Reader (ancestor of the Lan clan) as famous examples. The Lan clan's specialty is the Qimen arts: divination, geomancy, sigils, rattan figures and wards. Each year at Moonchase, evil spirits born of dead gods' remnants grow restless, and the Millelith work with civilian thaumaturges to suppress them.

Lan Yan explains that Qimen teaches the Ley Lines and human activity affect each other, so the eight "gates" (key Ley Line nodes) shift over time. She knows the Guyan sigils on Lantern Rite fortune coins, such as the Sign of Vaisravana, once an exorcism sigil and now a merchant's lucky charm. The "evil-dispelling technique" that every Liyue thaumaturge learns today began as the Wind Reader's private art. It spread because the Lan clan never turned away sincere students from other families.

12.content:
Lan Yan once lost track of time flying a kite and met Zibai on a hilltop. When she asked how the chariot flew, Zibai simply told her she was the White Horse Adeptus. In 7.1 Zibai recognised the soul-bound old man as "Mad Lan", who had once nicknamed her "White Foal", and confirmed he had cast the Soul-Binding on himself. Zhongli, whom Lan Yan knows only as the Wangsheng consultant, suggested the Moon-Viewing Gathering lead. After her art he told her the swallows were no longer rushing about.

Zhongli explained his knowledge by saying the Traveler had told him the story and that he knows Liyue's birds. Lan Yan thanked him and did not press further. Zibai has said both the Wind Reader and Silverwing would be delighted with how capable their descendants have become.

13.comment: Lan Yan: The Eight Adepts and Tao Dou
13.content:
The Eight Adepts were heroes who fought the god Tao Dou. The Three Beasts of Tao Dou (the Jade-Plumed Silverwing, the Lone Butterfly of the Crimson Flame and the Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare) were adepti. The Three Hermits of Guizang (the Wind Reader, the Wuwang Kid and the Yunlai Angler) and the Two Sages of Lianshan were human. Lan Yan has watched the operas about them many times, yet says the story never left a strong impression on her. People in her hometown still curse each other with "You'll never cross Mt. Tao Dou when you die."

In 7.1 the Wind Reader said the Eight met by chance at a roadside tea stand and decided to do some good, with no summons from Rex Lapis. Their nicknames survive in his memory: the Wuwang Kid was "Red Runt", the Yunlai Angler was "Fish Creel", Xiao was "Fairy Xiao" (Xiao declined to join), and Zibai's Third Deadly Self was "White Foal". The Yunlai Angler's descendant Jiangxue keeps a family rule to stay away from anyone like Mad Lan.

14.comment: Lan Yan: Chenyu Vale, Lan Yan's home ground
14.content:
Lan Yan knows the vale's tea slopes, cliffs and streams by heart. She guides lost travellers through the mists to Qiaoying Village, with its white walls and grey-tiled roofs. She has swum in every pool between Qiaoying and Mt. Lingmeng and loves the mists around Mt. Xuanlian and the smell of fresh-roasted tea. She rides Uncle Bosu's bamboo raft through Jademouth, and she knows a mountain eatery where guests bring their own ingredients. Her grandfather works in Yilong Wharf, where her clan hosted the 7.1 Moonchase.

Her idea of a perfect day is the life she already has: morning tea in a white-walled house, punting a bamboo raft while singing, weaving with a little dog at her side. Supper might be Tea-Smoked Squab. The night market sells grilled insects, which she cheerfully offers to guests. She hunts wild mushrooms with care and warns people about the hallucinogenic ones.
